# Standalone release verification

The Python checker uses only the standard library. Native compilation needs CMake 3.20+ and a C++17 compiler. The JavaScript reference smoke, included in a normal verification run, needs Node.js 22+. The optional WASM rebuild needs an installed Emscripten toolchain; the WASM ABI smoke alone works with Node.js 18.3+.

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
python3 tests/check_standalone_release.py \
  --source-zip releases/tetorica-soundchip-native-0.1.3-sources.zip \
  --wasm-zip releases/tetorica-soundchip-native-0.1.3-wasm.zip \
  --work-dir build/standalone-check \
  --build-wasm ym2612
```

The work directory must be empty. Its source tree is extracted from the ZIP, not copied from another checkout. Manifest inventories, hashes, source/license references, Native provenance, all 24 public SDK chips, all 29 WASM recipes and both JavaScript references are checked before building. MSM5205 and OKIM6295 are a separate JavaScript-only set: their entry points and source hashes must be present, their metadata must agree in both catalogs, and their Native/WASM status must remain `not-ported`. CMake File API and compiler-command paths reject outside project sources/includes. Downloading build recipes, external CMake fetches, archive symlinks and escaping paths are rejected. This is not an operating-system network sandbox; installed compiler/system headers and Emscripten's toolchain cache remain toolchain dependencies.

The standalone Native libraries cover YM2612/ymfm, YM2151/ymfm, YM2413/ymfm, YM2203/ymfm, YM2608/ymfm, YM2610/YM2610B/ymfm, Sega PSG, AY-3-8910, OKIM6258, RF5C164, Game Boy, HuC6280, NES with optional FDS, 32X PWM, MSFA DX7, SNES S-DSP, SPC700/S-DSP playback, WonderSwan, POKEY and YM3526/YM3812/YMF262/Y8950: twenty-four chip IDs plus the alternative Nuked YM2612 engine in twenty-one libraries; twenty-six aliases include generic `opl` and `nuked_ym2612`. Constructor kind/variant arguments select the actual core, independently of the alias/header. Normal verification builds all twenty-one static libraries and runs `tetorica.ym2612.self_test`, `tetorica.ym2151.self_test`, `tetorica.ym2413.self_test`, `tetorica.ym2203.self_test`, `tetorica.ym2608.self_test`, `tetorica.ym2610.self_test`, `tetorica.segapsg.self_test`, `tetorica.ay8910.self_test`, `tetorica.okim6258.self_test`, `tetorica.rf5c164.self_test`, `tetorica.opl.self_test`, `tetorica.extra_opl.self_test`, `tetorica.y8950_memory.self_test`, `tetorica.gameboy.self_test`, `tetorica.huc6280.self_test`, `tetorica.nes.self_test`, `tetorica.pwm.self_test`, `tetorica.extra_pwm.self_test`, `tetorica.dx7.self_test`, `tetorica.snes.self_test`, `tetorica.snes.extra_self_test`, `tetorica.spc.self_test`, `tetorica.nuked_ym2612.self_test` `tetorica.nuked_colink.self_test`, `tetorica.wonderswan.self_test` and `tetorica.pokey.self_test` through CTest, with assertions enabled in Release builds. The YM2151 fixture covers eight FM channels, pan, timers/status/IRQ, separate FM/CSM cancellation, Stop/reset and non-advancing observations, with allocation/free checks on the tested rendering paths. It does not instantiate X68000's OKIM6258 core. The independent PSG fixture covers three tone channels, noise, stereo, mute, clock edits, retained Stop/reset and observation without an OPLL or Genesis FM core. The YM2413 fixture covers nine melodic channels, built-in/user instruments, five rhythm aliases with physical-channel sharing, Stop/reset, cancellation, observation and deferred audition. The independent AY fixture covers three tones, shared noise/envelope, clock changes, synchronous readback, retained levels, Stop/reset and audition without allocating an OPLL sibling. The YM2203 fixture covers three FM plus three SSG voices, shared noise/envelope, prescalers, source/channel mutes, timers/status/IRQ, retained controls, separate FM/CSM cancellation and observation, including the primary/additional reset-history distinction. The YM2608 fixture checks FM/SSG/rhythm/ADPCM-B controls, fixed memory boundaries/copies/retention, raw CPU memory transfers, timers/status/IRQ, cancellation, observational snapshots and both constructor profiles. The shared YM2610 fixture checks both FM variants and both profiles, A/B dense ROM boundaries/copies, sparse-page ownership, retained memory/controls, Stop/reset, cancellation and observational status/state. The independent OKIM6258 fixture checks borrowed sample lifetime/replacement, low-nibble/FIFO continuity, clock/divider guards, pan, repeat, retained Stop/reset and non-advancing observation. The RF5C164 fixture checks both profiles, copied/banked RAM, markers, eight voices, clocks, reset/clear, ordinary mask-held timing and extra immediate cancellation/foreign-voice isolation. Three OPL-family fixtures cover primary chips/PCM/state, additional CSM/held cancellation/NEW/four-operator behavior, and Y8950 writable pages/CPU transfers/revisions/lifetime. A Y8950 snapshot avoids consuming ADPCM data or advancing audio, but its status read can propagate ADPCM flags into IRQ; PCM observation tests do not claim universal IRQ neutrality. The independent Game Boy fixture checks both pulses, owned wave RAM and noise, asymmetric NR50/NR51, source mute progression, retained Stop, clock/reset, invalid controls, state/ABI layout and zero allocation/free while rendering. Its 36 per-channel Stop cases span all four voices at 44.1/48/96 kHz and 100 kHz/base/100 MHz clocks, comparing exact foreign-voice PCM. Below the reference clock, per-channel Stop can retain the outer mixed sample until the next source frame; global Stop clears outer PCM immediately. Repeated state reads preserve PCM and strip trigger bits; reset restores the full DMG wave pattern while retaining edited clock/mute. The independent HuC6280 fixture checks the 352-byte state ABI, all six audible channels, copied/masked wave RAM, selection preservation and invalid-channel fallback, helper control/DDA restoration and phase effects, noise/LFO, mute progression, clock guards/reset retention and non-advancing observations. Its 120 stereo/foreign-voice Stop cases span all six sources at 8/44.1/48/96/384 kHz and 100 kHz/base/twice-base/100 MHz clocks; explicit low-clock tests retain both per-channel and global Stop outer PCM. Rendering checks reject allocation/free. The independent NES fixture checks the 400-byte state ABI, all six source gates/mutes, copied 64 KiB RAM, boundary/null uploads, DMC start/length/wrap/loop/IRQ and final-byte lifetime, protected host gates, FDS-off isolation, wave/modulation I/O gates and modulation, independent instances, regional tables, creation/clock guards, retained Stop and full reset. Repeated observations preserve state/PCM and IRQ flags. It checks the distinct I/O-disabled global/per-source FDS Stop contracts and exact final-byte DMC PCM/lifetime under unrelated gate edits; rendering and tested control paths allocate/free no C++ memory.

Two independent PWM fixtures cover primary FIFO depth/flags, routing, cycle/timer and duty integration, and additional-instance 64-bit ownership tags, overflow/collision cancellation, lifecycle and foreign-latch isolation. They also check constructor/clock guards, independent instances, retained Stop/reset, non-advancing snapshots and zero C++ allocation/free in tested render/control paths. PCM is compared with the retained reference core; direct shared-core DAC/gain/mute configuration checks do not imply those setters exist in the Native ABI.

The independent DX7 fixture checks accepted/rejected output rates, 16 held slots, mask-protected free slots and released tails, raw voice loading, same-identity held/released live edits, identity isolation, invalid-slot no-ops, release/kill buffered output, independent instances and one-time initialization. Panic must produce immediate silence and exact fresh-instance output for 96 feedback restart cases (all 32 algorithms at 44.1/48/96 kHz), guarding the SDK correction that resets preallocated note feedback history without allocation/free or changed addresses. Tested render/control paths reject C++ allocation/free.

The independent SNES fixture supplies `tetorica.snes.self_test` and `tetorica.snes.extra_self_test` from one executable. They check the 152-byte state ABI, 8–384 kHz rate guards, eight audible BRR voices with direct GAIN, same-frame KON merging, protected KON/KOFF bits, invalid register/channel no-ops, copied RAM and range guards, a stable owned RAM view across Stop/reset, reset's cleared RAM and nonzero muted DSP register image, retained sample/patch Stop, independent instances and exact PCM under repeated observations. The timeline checks use valid borrowed immutable RAM/DSP/event arrays and cover preparation/pause, restart copying, ordered events, completion, repeatable PCM and detachment on global Stop/reset. Tested rendering/control paths reject C++ allocation/free; invalid timeline arrays are caller errors, not a fixture safety claim. The immediate Stop-silence assertion uses disabled echo: retained echo RAM/volume may still produce output in other configurations. Separate actual-WASM comparisons exercise ADSR/GAIN modes, noise, pitch modulation, echo and output resampling; see [verification.md](../docs/verification.md).

The independent SPC fixture supplies `tetorica.spc.self_test` with a complete original SPC program/BRR dataset. It checks the 56-byte state and 16-byte event ABI, supported rates, copied loading, header/size rejection, successful-reload error recovery, pause/resume, bounded control-side seek, independent instances/mute, analysis purity, bounded event capture/overflow and tested allocation/free boundaries. A paused handle retains cached PCM and interpolation; mute is not assumed to clear existing 128-frame PCM or echo. Analysis snapshots are not full save states or complete SPC exports. Control-only create/load/seek/destroy operations occur before callback installation or after retirement; original file retention and publication are host responsibilities. See [verification.md](../docs/verification.md) for exact executed cases and Native/WASM comparison scope.

The checker also enables `TETORICA_NATIVE_BUILD_EXAMPLES`, requires `tetorica_genesis_wav`, `tetorica_master_system_wav`, `tetorica_msx_wav`, `tetorica_pc98_ym2203_wav`, `tetorica_pc98_ym2608_wav`, `tetorica_neogeo_wav`, `tetorica_x68000_wav`, `tetorica_megacd_wav`, `tetorica_dos_opl_wav`, `tetorica_msx_audio_wav`, `tetorica_gameboy_wav`, `tetorica_pcengine_wav`, `tetorica_nes_fds_wav`, `tetorica_32x_wav`, `tetorica_dx7_wav`, `tetorica_snes_wav`, `tetorica_spc_wav` `tetorica_nuked_genesis_wav`, `tetorica_wonderswan_wav` and `tetorica_pokey_wav`, and runs all twenty with selected output paths containing spaces. It checks each file's RIFF structure, 48 kHz stereo PCM16 format, complete frame count of at least one second, and nonzero, unclipped output on both channels. Each example produces 144,000 frames, links real chip libraries and generates its own notes/percussion. The MSX host combines AY and OPLL; the PC-98 hosts use YM2203 FM/SSG and YM2608 FM/SSG/rhythm/ADPCM-B, respectively. The NeoGeo host uses all four YM2610 physical FM slots, SSG and ADPCM-A/B. The X68000 host combines a separate YM2151 and OKIM6258, keeping its borrowed synthetic ADPCM buffer alive beyond the decoder. The Mega-CD host combines YM2612, Sega PSG and primary RF5C164 with a copied looping PCM waveform. The DOS host selects OPL/OPL2/OPL3 in three one-second sections with rhythm and an OPL3 stereo four-operator pair; MSX-AUDIO mixes Y8950 FM/ADPCM-B with AY/OPLL and retains writable pages beyond the decoder lifetime. The Game Boy host uses both pulses, an original wave-RAM triangle and noise, with left/right isolation followed by a combined phrase at the 4,194,304 Hz clock. The PC Engine host generates original triangle/sine/pulse waves, host-fed 5-bit DDA and both noise channels at 3,579,545 Hz, with left/right phrases and a final six-source mix. The NES/FDS host uses both pulses, triangle, noise and copied original DMC bits, then an original FDS wave, then all six at the 1,789,773 Hz NTSC base clock; mono output is duplicated to stereo. The 32X host first isolates original PWM PCM/percussion left then right, then mixes PWM with separate YM2612/PSG cores. It uses the exact 23,011,361 Hz Native clock, cycle 960, neutral duty 480 and 959-clock source ticks; a bounded three-entry FIFO feeder fills only free slots. The DX7 host constructs original 155-byte six-operator voices with algorithms 1/5/32, a same-identity live timbre edit, a C-major chord and explicit note-slot releases; the retained 44.1 kHz core is interpolated to 48 kHz and its mono signal is duplicated into stereo. The SNES host copies original sine/triangle/pulse BRR loops into owned RAM, isolates a left sine and right ADSR triangle, then uses all eight voices in a stereo chord with ADSR/direct GAIN and explicit KOFF releases. It derives pitch from the fixed 32 kHz source rate, not the 48 kHz output, and disables echo writes. The SPC host constructs an original SPC700 program and three BRR loops in a complete SPC file. Timer 0 drives CPU-written DSP melody/chord/KOFF events; a bounded observer verifies writes while the host only loads/starts/samples. Fixed gain and edge fades preserve output headroom. The sample examples generate original data rather than loading hardware/game ROM contents. No audio device or external sample assets are used. Fixed example mix gains do not alter library defaults or model motherboard analog mixing.

Standalone Node ABI smokes are provided for YM2612/ymfm, WonderSwan and POKEY. Source/WASM release manifests and build-info identify which artifacts were actually included and built; other chips retain their explicitly recorded verification/license status. The Node smoke tests synchronous reads, audible finite stereo output, reset and exact PCM continuation after save/load. It loads the supplied loader unchanged through a temporary `.mjs` file, with explicit WASM bytes and no npm dependencies.

The checker selects Release explicitly for single- and multi-configuration CMake generators. It requires all twenty-five Native fixture executables and twenty WAV example artifacts in CMake's File API, supports Windows `.exe` paths and spaces, and audits relative compiler paths and MSVC include options. `--work-dir` may be absolute or relative to the invocation directory. The directory must be empty.

The [CI workflow](../.github/workflows/verify-sdk.yml) is configured to run all twenty-six Native CTest tests, twenty WAV examples and the JavaScript verification on Windows, Linux, and macOS, including Linux ARM64 and both Mac architectures. Three Ubuntu jobs separately build and audit the YM2612, WonderSwan and POKEY WASM releases and repeats the WASM build/smoke using its extracted source ZIP. Completed runs and their exact target scope are recorded in [verification.md](../docs/verification.md).

The JavaScript smoke imports the copied engines from the extracted source tree and checks audible finite stereo output, exact chunk continuity, mute progression, reset, MSM5205 external VCLK, OKIM6295 sample/voice commands, stop/end behavior and attachment gain. It also runs the synthetic rendering example from a temporary directory and verifies both PCM16 WAV files. No npm installation, browser or audio device is used.

To recheck unchanged releases without compiling again, pass `--audit-only --wasm-smoke --javascript-smoke`. With just `--audit-only`, no compiler or Node process is started. To run either smoke directly:

```sh
node tests/wasm_smoke.mjs /path/to/extracted-release/wasm
node tests/wonderswan_wasm_smoke.mjs /path/to/extracted-release/wasm
node tests/pokey_wasm_smoke.mjs /path/to/extracted-release/wasm
node tests/javascript_reference_smoke.mjs /path/to/extracted-source/reference/javascript
```

The Nuked fixture preserves the original Native event/PCM/status CLI and checks
both raw and Native synchronous APIs. A test-only instrumented wrapper object
counts C malloc/free as well as C++ new/delete on tested rendering/control paths;
production libraries have no audit hooks. The coexistence fixture links regular
ymfm YM2612, Nuked and PSG, starts eight independent cold constructors in
parallel, then checks regular-engine PCM while changing Nuked state. It never
shares one handle concurrently. The Nuked offline example renders the same
original Genesis sketch through Nuked FM plus separate PSG; it is not a machine
emulator or an analog-mix measurement.

The POKEY fixture checks four-channel sound, raw volume-only gain/clipping, actual read-side I/O, immediate monitor mute with phase progression, deterministic reset, multiple constructor clocks/output rates and exact render partitions. Two handles with different clock/noise programs are interleaved against isolated references; muting, resetting, destroying or recreating the first must preserve the second's PCM and read I/O exactly. Its tested hot controls/rendering allocate no C++ `new`/`new[]` memory; this counter does not intercept arbitrary C `malloc`. The standalone WASM smoke exercises two handles sharing one module heap. `tests/check_pokey_core.mjs` accepts the real native fixture and WASM directory for exact cross-backend comparisons without npm or an audio device.

`tetorica_pokey_wav output.wav` renders two POKEYs to centered mono at an explicit `0.5/0.5` host mix. Appending `--stereo` places one physical chip on each side. The example's documented DC blocker and file fades affect only listening output; raw-core Native/WASM checks retain positive mono PCM and legacy `/32768` gain. No game music/ROM or motherboard analog-mix measurement is supplied.

For POKEY cross-backend checking without building all other cores a second time, pass `--audit-only --pokey-native-parity --wasm-smoke --build-wasm pokey` together with a source and POKEY WASM ZIP. The checker audits the extracted CMake source inventory, builds only the discovered POKEY fixture target, and runs exact Native/WASM comparison against both the archived and independently rebuilt artifact. Full Native verification also runs this comparison automatically when its supplied WASM archive contains POKEY. A plain `--audit-only` still starts no compiler or Node process.
